quote: we try to look for the best business models in the world and we have been following
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Starts from business model quality; follows companies for years before acting.

quote: the story with her Isaac was a dominant franchise it scores business is one of the highest quality
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Fair Isaac (FICO); scores business called one of highest-quality business models.

quote: there wasn't a lot of organic growth during the early years of the company its growth was completely related to volume and there was really no change to pricing of its course product but that changed in 2018 which got us interested in the company
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: FICO. Lesson: a change in pricing behaviour (organic growth) made a dominant franchise investable.

quote: even if a FICO score costs 10 times more let's say five dollars it still offers tremendous value
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: FICO. Price small relative to loan size and value delivered means room to raise prices.

quote: that's an important part of businesses that we like at our firm is having businesses that still have a tremendous amount of operating leverage
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Likes businesses whose margins can still rise; FICO ebit margin about 40 percent.

quote: importantly the business model is extremely Capital light
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Capital-light model valued; FICO capex under 10 million on 20 billion market cap.

quote: the company has had less than 10 million dollars in capex to support a company whose market cap is approaching 20 billion dollars that is absolutely incredible
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: FICO. Capital-light plus operating leverage makes it special.

quote: what you'd like to see is a business that does not have to make defensive Acquisitions does not have to reinvest heavily in the business to keep it going
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Capital allocation test: no defensive acquisitions, low reinvestment needed to keep dominance.

quote: the company has required 20 of its outstanding shares over the last five years and 25 over the last 10 years it's really an amazing use of capital
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: FICO bought back about 20 percent of shares in 5 years; captions say 'required' for acquired.

quote: and that you don't have to invest a lot to maintain its dominance and you don't need to buy businesses to protect your franchise
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: FICO. Free cash flow goes to buybacks because dominance needs little investment.

quote: there's always a bear case for any company so many investors worried about the synchrony transition
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Bear cases always exist; FICO bear cases listed: Synchrony, VantageScore, FHFA, antitrust, AI.

quote: we don't invest in businesses where you have to twist somebody's Farm to use the product or service
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Avoids products customers are forced to use; end users must derive real benefit.

quote: we believe in what we call Natural monopolies or oligopolies
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Natural monopolies or oligopolies from user benefit and network effects.

quote: because the score is so cheap relative to the loan decisions being made there is just a tremendous runway for pricing power that still delivers exceeding value
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: FICO. Cheap relative to decisions it informs gives pricing power runway.

quote: what I like about this business is you're not forcing anybody to use the score everyone can go out tomorrow and use Vantage score
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: FICO. Voluntary use; same lesson as no forced products.

quote: I've always said that two kids in a dorm room at MIT could come up with an equivalent mathematical model for credit scoring but that's not what matters what matters is the networking effect
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Moat is the network effect, not the technology itself.

quote: there's been many opportunities to buy the company at depressed levels over the last five years because of some of the items like the fhfa decision or what was happening with synchrony
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: FICO. Regulatory and customer-loss fears created depressed prices; implies buying on such fears.

quote: arguably today based on its growth profile we don't really believe in some of the parts at our firm
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Does not value by sum of the parts.

quote: it's in a dominant Market position tremendous pricing power provides great value for the price of its product long runway for pricing power operating leverage not a lot in the way of reinvestment a natural networking effect
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Ideal-business checklist: dominant position, pricing power, value for price, operating leverage, low reinvestment, network effect.

quote: I look at the crop of IPOs and specs there's almost a thousand of them that came to Market over the last few years we have not been able to identify a single one whose business model is as compelling
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Recent IPOs and SPACs judged less compelling than FICO; few new businesses meet the bar.

quote: we like to be great historians of companies we were following this company for a long time knew of its dominant position we were worried about its organic growth profile
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Studies a company's history over a long time before investing.

quote: and then we realized that there was a change happening that many others in the marketplace may not have realized
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: FICO 2018. Lesson: acts when a change in the business (pricing) removes the known worry.

quote: the investment business is about looking forward in assessing future risk and future growth
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Looking forward, assessing future risk and growth.

quote: near-term share price volatility doesn't bother us at all it actually gives us the opportunity to buy into great businesses
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Uses share-price volatility to buy great businesses.

quote: the more volatility that these companies have the better for long-term investors like us
speaker: Dev Kantesaria
note: Volatility in great businesses favours long-term buyers.
